b9e36f97ff2234d5: ZURICH: Influential investors in Swiss chocolate maker Lindt & Spruengli are calling for sweeping boardroom changes at the maker of Lindor truffles after pricing missteps hammered the share price and led to the ousting of its CEO last month.

The criticism, based on interviews with five major investors including three top-20 shareholders, adds to pressure on Lindt as it searches for a new CEO. Its shares are down about a quarter this year after outlook cuts and weak performance in Europe.

After Lindt ousted CEO Adalbert Lechner following two sales warnings this year, the shareholders said they wanted the board refreshed and the powers of Chairman Ernst Tanner, 80, curbed. Tanner has been chairman for 32 years, and executive chairman since 2016.

"Renewal cannot stop at the executive management. It should also happen on the board," said Ingo Speich of Lindt investor Deka, adding that the Swiss firm faced structural challenges that required "new thinking."
"The current concentration of power must be abolished," added Speich.
Of the five investors Reuters spoke to, only one large shareholder backed the company's current board. Six other major shareholders contacted by Reuters declined to comment.

The comments mark the first major rebuke of Lindt's board since Lechner's ouster last month. Tanner has faced opposition before, with some shareholders voting against his reelection at annual meetings in recent years.
Lindt said the board had launched the search for a new CEO and expected to appoint a successor in the second quarter of 2027. Lechner could not be reached for comment. Tanner declined to comment.
"The board also reviews the board composition regularly," a Lindt spokesperson said. "Succession planning is a fixed part of its work."
'THE WORLD HAS CHANGED'
Lindt ran into difficulties this year after raising prices in response to soaring cocoa costs, hitting sales volumes as consumers tightened their belts.
Tanner acknowledged last month that Lindt had misjudged consumers' willingness to pay after hiking prices by 19 per cent in 2025 and a further 12 per cent in the first half of 2026.

The company cut its organic growth forecast to between 0 per cent and 2 per cent, well below the 10.9 per cent five-year average. Germany head Michal Spiller left alongside Lechner, with former CEO Dieter Weisskopf returning as interim CEO.
Spiller could not be reached for comment.
Vincent Kaufmann, CEO of Ethos, Switzerland's leading shareholder advisory group, said Lindt suffered from a lack of adequate checks and balances on its supervisory board.

"The search for a new CEO is a first step ... However, a change of CEO alone will not resolve the governance issues Ethos has raised, which concern the board itself," Kaufmann said, adding that only three of the board's eight members were independent according to its criteria while company pension funds were overrepresented.

One top-20 shareholder, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the board shared responsibility for the pricing missteps and needed new blood, noting that six of its eight members were at least 70 years old and that Tanner had served as chairman since 1994.
Lindt owed Tanner a great deal, the investor said, but "the world has changed greatly over the past 30 years."

Tanner has said he won't step down, saying his priority is to get the company back on track. He remains strongly placed, personally holding 2.3 per cent of the company's shares, while two pension funds he chairs have more than 15 per cent of the voting rights.
A second top-20 investor said he understood why Tanner was staying and defended the price increases, which were key to protecting margins at the US$24 billion company.
Lindt reaffirmed its medium- to long-term goal of 6 per cent to 8 per cent annual sales growth, though investors say achieving it could prove challenging.

A third top-20 investor said it could be difficult for the company to quickly recapture previous growth rates, with challenges around pricing and the rise of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, which could curb chocolate consumption.

16fde8cfceb67ec4: SUNGAI BULOH: Flash floods have inundated several areas around Sungai Buloh, forcing full and partial road closures, while floodwaters entered homes and a mosque in Bandar Seri Coalfields today.
Among the worst-affected locations is Masjid At-Taufiqiah in Bandar Seri Coalfields, where floodwaters rose to waist level, submerging its prayer halls and surrounding compound.
Photographs from the scene showed muddy brown water covering the mosque's floors, with debris and silt carried into the building.
Several men were also seen wading through waist-deep water inside the mosque as floodwaters continued to inundate the premises.
Aerial footage showed muddy floodwaters surrounding the mosque, with vehicles lining an adjacent road.
Separate footage showed a long stretch of road submerged, with traffic cones marking sections of the flooded route.
Masjid At-Taufiqiah Bandar Seri Coalfields deputy chairman Muhammad Nur Ariff Mohd Sadni said water levels began rising at 7am and had receded only slightly as of 12.32pm.
"This mosque is affected by floods every year. It has been a regular occurrence since 2017," he told the New Straits Times.
He said mosque officials were waiting for the floodwaters to subside before beginning cleaning operations.
"We are waiting for the waters to recede so that we can begin cleaning the mosque.

"It is important that we clean the premises immediately once the water has fully subsided because the silt brought in by the floodwaters will harden if left to dry, making it much more difficult to remove," he said.
Meanwhile, Jeram assemblyman Datuk Harrison Hassan said flooding had also disrupted traffic along several major roads in the surrounding areas.
He said the traffic light intersection at Bukit Cherakah and Bandar Seri Coalfields remained closed due to high floodwaters.
"The LATAR Puncak Alam-Sungai Buloh exit is also partially submerged at the moment," he said.
Harrison said Taman Saujana Aman was also affected, with floodwaters reaching ankle level inside most houses.
He said water levels at the entrance to the residential area had reached knee height.

Meanwhile, Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the affected areas included Kampung Melayu Subang, Kampung Paya Jaras, Jalan Kubu Gajah and Lorong Sembilan in Sungai Buloh.
Other affected locations were Taman Industri Jaya in Ijok, Jalan Seri Ajwa in Section U17, Shah Alam, and the Bukit Jelutong toll plaza area.
Ashrul said water levels across all affected locations were showing a downward trend.
He said rain had started at midnight and continued until shortly after 4am.
Harrison said the Kuala Selangor Municipal Council (MPKS) hall in Desa Coalfields had been opened for members of the public and flood victims seeking refuge.

784692a4ce2de229: KUALA LUMPUR: A meeting of Malaysian development expertise and Japanese real estate pedigree is set to reshape the premium residential landscape in Kuala Lumpur, with Paramount Corporation Bhd joining forces with Mitsui Fudosan (Asia) Malaysia Sdn Bhd to develop The Ashbourne, a RM1.3 billion residential project in the prestigious U-Thant enclave.

The strategic joint venture brings together two property players with complementary strengths, combining Paramount's established foothold in the Kuala Lumpur market with Mitsui Fudosan's international experience in delivering high-quality residential developments.
Under the partnership, Mitsui Fudosan will acquire a 49 per cent equity interest in Meridian Kuasa Sdn Bhd for RM23.1 million, while Paramount will retain a controlling 51 per cent stake.
Currently wholly owned by Paramount, Meridian Kuasa will serve as the joint venture vehicle for The Ashbourne, with Paramount taking the lead in project management, sales and marketing.
The partnership was formalised today through the signing of a suite of agreements, marking a significant milestone in Paramount's expansion strategy in the capital.

Paramount Corporation group chief executive officer Jeffrey Chew said the acquisition of the development land earlier this year was a strategic move to deepen the group's presence in Kuala Lumpur's city centre.

"We are pleased to welcome Mitsui Fudosan as our strategic partner in The Ashbourne. Its 49 per cent investment reflects our shared confidence in the potential of this development and brings together complementary strengths," Chew said.
"Beyond the financial investment, the partnership reinforces The Ashbourne's positioning in the premium residential market and provides opportunities to reach a wider international audience."

He said Mitsui Fudosan brought extensive international real estate experience, global market reach and expertise in high-quality residential developments, while Paramount contributed deep local market knowledge, development capabilities and a proven execution track record.
"Together, we aim to create an exceptional residential offering that draws on the best of both organisations while laying the groundwork for future collaboration," Chew said.
Set on 3.7 acres of freehold commercial development land off Jalan Ampang, The Ashbourne will comprise two towers housing 458 high-end serviced residences.

With built-up areas ranging from approximately 1,491 sq ft to 2,661 sq ft, the development is designed to appeal to discerning homeowners seeking privacy, space and convenience in one of Kuala Lumpur's established residential addresses.
Each residence will feature a private lift lobby, reinforcing the development's emphasis on exclusivity and privacy.
Conceived around the principles of quiet refinement and effortless urban living, The Ashbourne is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2030.

For Paramount, the project represents more than a substantial addition to its development pipeline. It builds on a track record in the Jalan Ampang-Kuala Lumpur city centre corridor, where its earlier developments, The Ashwood and The Atrium, were fully sold.

The latest venture underscores the group's strategy of pursuing locations where it has established market credentials and sees sustainable demand, while leveraging strategic partnerships to strengthen its development capabilities and market reach.
For Mitsui Fudosan, meanwhile, the collaboration represents an opportunity to deepen its participation in Malaysia's property market through a partnership with an established local developer.
Its managing director, Masayoshi Saito, said the company was excited to embark on its first collaboration with Paramount Corporation through The Ashbourne.
"The Ashbourne reflects our confidence in the market and our commitment to long-term investment in the country," he said.

"By combining Paramount's proven local expertise with Mitsui Fudosan's residential development experience in Japan and internationally, we look forward to delivering a distinctive, high-quality living environment that creates long-term value for residents and the surrounding community."

b248ab4722d2bcfc: KUALA LUMPUR: National interim coach Tan Cheng Hoe has defended his decision to omit Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) players from his 24-man squad for friendlies in China, citing the club's congested November schedule.

Cheng Hoe said the exclusion was necessary after considering JDT's commitments in the Asian Champions League Elite (ACLE), Asean Club Championship, and FA Cup semi-finals, while recognising the importance of the club's continental campaign to Malaysia's AFC Member Association (MA) ranking.
JDT are scheduled to play four matches this month, and Cheng Hoe said giving them room to manage their workload could eventually benefit Malaysian football.
"Besides giving JDT room to manage their congested schedule, I have also considered the importance of allowing them to focus fully on their continental commitments.
"JDT have an opportunity to add more points to Malaysia's MA ranking, which will benefit the country's standing in Asian football," he said.
Cheng Hoe said the absence of several JDT regulars has opened the door for other players to stake their claims ahead of the 2030 World Cup-2032 Asian Cup qualifying campaign.

Of the 24 players selected, 11 featured in Malaysia's FIFA Asean Cup campaign this year in Indonesia, while another 11 have earned recalls, including three who also represented the national team in the Hyundai Asean Cup.
Harimau Malaya will face hosts China on Nov 14 before playing Yemen three days later at the Zhaoqing New District Sports Centre Stadium in Guangdong.
"For these two friendlies in China, I have decided to give more players an opportunity, including two new faces in the national squad.
"I want to see their ability, quality and suitability for international football, as well as how well they adapt to our playing style and the team's requirements," he said.

With the next FIFA international window not scheduled until March, Cheng Hoe said it was important to make full use of the China tour to assess his options, build partnerships, and strengthen the team's tactical understanding.

e43cf6af95b2598e: SINGAPORE, Nov 4 — Nanyang Technological University (NTU) students have launched a petition urging the university to protect vendors at CresPion Canteen, as a change in management threatens to displace existing stalls.
Titled “Save Our CresPion Canteen”, students are concerned that rising rental costs and renovation fees imposed by the incoming operator could force vendors to shut down or relocate.
As of yesterday, it has garnered 1,533 signatures on Change.org.
The student group NTU Financial Aid and Friends also shared the petition on Instagram, highlighting concerns over the potential loss of affordable food options on campus.
NTU’s Office of Commercial and Auxiliary Services (OCAS) is changing the canteen’s operator to Food Paradise, with renovation scheduled to begin on December 11.

According to the petition, every existing stall is currently facing the possibility of having to quit, with vendors having to decide whether they can afford to continue operating under the new arrangements.
Vendors face up to two to three times increase in monthly costs
The petition states that existing vendors currently pay around S$3,600 (RM11,452) in monthly costs to the outgoing operator, Food Haven.
This includes rental, cleaning and management fees, as well as the Gross Turnover (GTO), which refers to a percentage of a stall’s monthly sales paid to the landlord on top of its base rent.

According to the petition, which cites figures obtained through interviews with stakeholders who wish to remain anonymous, monthly costs under the new arrangement are expected to exceed S$7,100, in addition to a 5 per cent GTO.
Vendors will also have to fork out an additional S$20,000 in renovation fees, the petition claimed. It amounts to more than five months of their previous rent.
The students felt that the increased operating costs could eventually translate into higher food prices or force existing vendors to leave.
“These vendors are the heartbeat of CresPion, providing relatively affordable meals to students who reside here and in neighbouring halls,” the petition stated.
It added that replacing the existing stalls with new operators could result in more expensive food options, further limiting access to affordable meals on campus.
Students call on NTU to protect existing vendors
The petition outlines four demands for NTU OCAS, including allowing existing vendors to remain without having to bear the additional renovation costs and steep rental increases.
It also calls for the university to keep rental and food costs affordable, arguing that higher operating expenses could eventually be passed on to students and other customers.
“Currently, there are no other alternatives as cheap as what CresPion Canteen offers,” the petition stated.
The students pointed out that vendors already experience up to four months of reduced income during school holidays, when student traffic on campus is lower.
They also urged NTU to reconsider what they described as profit-maximising practices, arguing that the university, as a public institution, should prioritise the welfare of its students and workers.
AsiaOne has reached out to NTU for more information. — AsiaOne

c570d30b8e78751d: PETALING JAYA: Pelabur asing perlu memainkan peranan lebih besar dalam membangunkan keupayaan syarikat dan tenaga kerja tempatan, bukan hanya membawa masuk modal serta teknologi ke Malaysia, kata Timbalan Perdana Menteri, Fadillah Yusof.

Jelasnya, aspek pemindahan teknologi, pembangunan pembekal tempatan dan latihan tenaga kerja berkemahiran perlu menjadi antara keutamaan pelabur asing bagi memastikan manfaat pelaburan dapat dinikmati dalam jangka panjang.

"Saya mengharapkan lebih banyak syarikat dan pelabur dari luar apabila melabur di Malaysia, bukan saja mencari rakan kongsi tempatan, tetapi melibatkan keseluruhan rantaian nilai, daripada aspek pembekalan dan sebagainya serta memberi keutamaan kepada orang tempatan.

"Pada masa sama, mereka perlu melatih tenaga tempatan supaya kita dapat melaksanakan pemindahan teknologi dan meninggalkan sesuatu yang berkekalan di negara ini," katanya menurut Sinar Harian ketika berucap merasmikan Persidangan Tahunan Jawatankuasa Penjanaan Kuasa Turbin Gas CGNEI 2026 di Pusat Latihan EPH, Loji Janakuasa Edra Melaka di Alor Gajah.

Fadillah berkata, kerjasama jangka panjang dengan syarikat antarabangsa mampu memberi manfaat lebih besar, jika disertai perkongsian pengalaman operasi, kepakaran dan pembangunan keupayaan syarikat tempatan.

Menteri peralihan tenaga dan transformasi air berkata, peningkatan keupayaan tempatan bukan saja mengukuhkan industri tenaga negara, Malaysia juga boleh memainkan peranan lebih besar dalam memperkukuh keselamatan tenaga serantau.

Sementara itu, katanya, pusat latihan yang diwujudkan menerusi inisiatif CGN dan Edra Power Holdings berpotensi menjadi platform melahirkan lebih ramai pakar dalam bidang operasi penjanaan tenaga, khasnya teknologi turbin gas.

"Ini penting untuk melatih tenaga kerja di Malaysia supaya mereka bukan saja menjadi pekerja mahir, tetapi akhirnya dapat meningkatkan pendapatan. Mereka juga telah bersetuju membuka peluang ini bukan saja kepada Melaka, tetapi untuk seluruh Malaysia."

999a16ed496fa90e: KOTA BARU: A teacher was charged in the Sessions Court here today with two counts of sexually assaulting a male pupil in a hostel warden's room in Dabong, Kuala Krai, last year.
Mohd Faiz Rohizat, 34, who is also a hostel warden at the primary school, pleaded not guilty after both charges were read before judge Zulkifli Abllah.

According to the charges, the accused allegedly physically sexually assaulted the boy, who was 11 years old at the time of the incidents, inside the hostel warden's room of the school in Dabong, Kuala Krai, near here at 1pm in April 2025 and at 4pm in September 2025.

The first charge was framed under Section 14(b) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, while the second charge was framed under Section 14(d) of the same act. Both sections provide for a prison sentence of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Syazalia Che Suhaimin prosecuted, while counsel Siti Fathma Nuraimi Mohamad represented the accused.
Earlier, Syazalia did not offer bail, citing the severity of the alleged offences.
In mitigation, Siti Fathma pleaded for bail, submitting that the accused is a civil servant with a wife and a 3-year-old child.
"The accused will lose his job and source of income if bail is denied, and my client needs to support his wife, child, and ailing parents.
"As a civil servant, the accused poses no flight risk since he resides at a permanent address in Bachok," she said.

The court allowed bail at RM10,000 with one surety, alongside additional conditions requiring the accused to provide a permanent residential address and refrain from harassing prosecution witnesses and the victim.
The court also ordered the accused to report to the nearest police station once every two months and surrender his passport to the court.
The court fixed Dec 23 for case mention.
3c158a1e9696712e: SUNGAI BULOH: A bridge along Jalan Kubu Gajah collapsed early this morning following heavy rain, completely cutting off the main road connecting Kampung Kubu Gajah and Paya Jaras Hilir.

The incident, believed to have occurred at 2am, was caused by strong currents in Sungai Subang following heavy rainfall. The currents eroded the riverbank and compromised the bridge's structural stability.
The Petaling district Public Works Department (PWD), in a statement today, said 48mm of rainfall was recorded at the Paya Jaras Hilir monitoring station.
"The strong currents in Sungai Subang following heavy rain caused damage to the riverbank near the bridge, affecting the stability of the structure," it said.
The collapse left a large section of the road severely damaged, with photographs showing the asphalt surface torn apart and parts of the road having fallen into the riverbank below.
The department said the affected stretch had been completely closed to all vehicles to ensure public safety.
A traffic management plan has been prepared and implemented, including the installation of warning signs, safety barriers and diversion signs.
Motorists heading towards Merbau Sempak and Kubu Gajah have been advised to use Jalan Merbau Sempak towards Masjid Nurul Iman.
Those travelling to Paya Jaras Hilir can still access the area via Jalan Paya Jaras Hilir from Federal Route 54 (FT54).
The department said a temporary Bailey bridge would be installed as a medium-term measure to restore connectivity between the affected areas.
A permanent bridge will eventually be constructed to replace the collapsed structure.
The incident comes amid heavy rainfall that triggered flooding in several areas around Sungai Buloh early today, resulting in road closures and the opening of temporary evacuation centres.
The affected bridge is located along a state road crossing Sungai Subang in the Petaling district.

“Banyak perkara telah kita lakukan dan akan diteruskan seperti biasa. Perkara yang masih dalam perancangan dan memerlukan usaha berterusan akan kita gandakan usaha.
“Ini bagi memastikan harapan masyarakat di Kuala Linggi dipenuhi sebaik mungkin,” katanya.
034c72821fe6f337: KUALA LUMPUR: A Taiwanese karaoke centre manager pleaded not guilty at the magistrate's court to driving under the influence of drugs and causing injuries to a police escort rider attached to the entourage of Negri Sembilan Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir last Saturday.

Wei Fu-Chun, 52, was charged with driving a car under the influence of drugs, rendering him incapable of exercising proper control of a Mercedes-Benz and causing injuries to Corporal Samsul Rahimi Sapari, 42.
He was alleged to have committed the offence at 8.50pm along Jalan Tun Sambanthan on Oct 31.
The charge, under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act, carries a jail term of between seven and 10 years and a fine of between RM30,000 and RM50,000 upon conviction.
Wei entered his plea before magistrate Aliaa Anwar.
Deputy public prosecutor Nurbatrisyia Mohd Razib did not offer bail due to concerns that Wei was a foreigner without a permanent address in Malaysia.
She also informed the court that details of his proposed bailor were incomplete.
Defence lawyer Thayalan Moorthy told the court that he would seek further instructions from his client on whether to file a bail application.
Aliaa denied bail and fixed Jan 6 for the submission of documents.
The incident occurred while Samsul, who is attached to the city Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) motorcycle unit, was returning from escort duty.
Wei allegedly crashed his car into Samsul, leaving him with injuries to his legs and hands.
He attempted to flee but was detained by another motorcycle unit policeman.
City TEID chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said a breathalyser test conducted on Wei returned a negative result for alcohol.
However, drugs believed to be ecstasy were found in the vehicle.
e17669c531243ddf: SHAH ALAM: Three siblings had to seek assistance from the Fire and Rescue Department to evacuate their bedridden mother after floodwaters rose rapidly to waist level at Kampung Paya Jaras Hilir, Sungai Buloh, early today.
Nur Nazihah Asyiqin Mohd Said, 27, said they had not expected the water to rise so quickly and had to call the Fire and Rescue Department to help move their 60-year-old mother to safety.
She said their house was in a flood-prone area, but the water usually rose gradually.
She said it started raining around 10pm yesterday as she returned from work, and she was initially not too concerned until the downpour intensified around midnight.
"At 2am, my younger sibling woke me up and said water was rushing into the house.
"We initially thought it would not rise too high, but by 3am, it had reached my waist.
"As I was worried about my mother, who is bedridden following a stroke, I asked my brother to seek help to get her to safety.
"The fire and rescue team arrived at 3.30am and took us to the Sinar Pagi temporary relief centre," she said when contacted today.
Nur Nazihah Asyiqin said she had lived in the house with her mother, brother and younger brother for 25 years, and flooding was not new to them.
She said their house was also flooded to waist level around April last year, damaging many of their belongings.
This time, however, they managed to salvage only a few items as the water rose too quickly. They also did not have time to save their mother's medication.
Although floodwaters around their house have receded, she said the family had decided to remain at the relief centre for fear that the water could rise again if it rained.
"I was told that the Social Welfare Department would help us obtain medication for my mother.
"I briefly returned home to collect some clothes. Although the floodwaters had receded, we could not clean the house as we had to attend to my mother.
"What worries me most is the possibility of another flood, as I understand it may rain again this afternoon.
"Although my mother seems uncomfortable at the relief centre, we have no choice. Her safety is more important," she said.
4c1b11f8b7ee5587: PETALING JAYA: A mother and daughter who obstructed Muar municipal council (MPM) enforcement officers during an operation to catch stray dogs last month were fined RM500 each by the Muar magistrates' court today.
Ainun Jongin, 52, an Indonesian national, and her daughter, Loo Sock Yan, 24, pleaded guilty after the charges were read out before magistrate Kartini Kasran, reported Berita Harian.
The court also ordered them to serve 30 days in jail if they failed to pay the fines. Both women paid the fines.

According to the charges, the two jointly and intentionally obstructed a public servant, a 31-year-old MPM assistant public health officer, from carrying out his duties during an operation to catch stray dogs.
The offence took place in front of a house in Taman Bintang Emas, Bukit Pasir, at 5.45am on Oct 29.

They were charged under Section 186 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code, which provides for a jail term of up to two years, a maximum fine of RM10,000 or both, upon conviction.
According to the facts of the case, the complainant, who was also the victim, led an integrated operation to catch stray dogs around Taman Bintang Emas, Bukit Pasir.
The enforcement team found several dogs roaming the area and managed to catch two dogs before the mother and daughter obstructed the complainant by attempting to free the animals.
The complainant warned them not to interfere with the enforcement officers' duties and informed them that owners could claim the captured dogs at the MPM office.
However, the women took the equipment used to catch the dogs. A female enforcement officer attempted to intervene and alleviate the situation but fell during the incident.
Deputy public prosecutor Yasmin Piah prosecuted, while the two women were represented by lawyer Tan Joes Nan.
353f0a14f3efc4b6: KUALA LUMPUR: A Bersatu MP today hit out at PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang for comparing the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) signed between the government and seven opposition MPs to the Dajjal's deception.
Suhaimi Abdullah (PN-Langkawi), who was among the six MPs from Bersatu who signed the CSA last week, described the comparison as "grave" and detrimental to national unity.
"How can we (as a nation) foster unity if opposition MPs are labelled 'Dajjal'? This is unfortunate," he said when debating the 2027 budget.
Suhaimi also said his children had quizzed him about the Dajjal.
"I said I wasn't sure and that I was looking into it."
The Dajjal is the great deceiver whose emergence is regarded in Islam as one of the major signs of the approaching Day of Judgment. He is also sometimes referred to as the anti-Christ.
In drawing the parallel yesterday, Hadi said Prophet Muhammad had warned that before the emergence of the great Dajjal, several "lesser Dajjals" would appear throughout the world.

"A CSA is Dajjal-like as power is no longer regarded as a trust that must be upheld for the benefit of all, but instead becomes a means of coercing others to ensure the government remains in power," the Marang MP was quoted as saying.
The CSA will provide access to constituency development funds that government MPs have had access to for the past four years.

It also underlines two key reforms for Putrajaya to undertake in exchange for the MPs' support: limiting the prime minister's tenure and separating the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor before the end of the parliamentary term.

The other five MPs from Bersatu who signed the agreement were Muhyiddin Yassin (Pagoh), Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Ali Biju (Saratok), Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai). Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman also signed the CSA.
3562270318266c7e: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 4 — A Court of Appeal judge has advised celebrity preacher Da’I Syed, whose real name is Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohd Shaiful, not to abuse his popularity or take advantage of vulnerable individuals.
Judge Datuk Azman Abdullah, who chaired a three-member panel, said exploiting individuals who were emotionally vulnerable could tarnish the reputation of those who projected a religious image.

“I would like to offer some advice to the appellant. This advice is not directed solely at you. We often come across cases involving rape, sodomy and similar offences occurring at pondok (religious) schools, allegedly committed by teachers...this reflects poorly on society,” he said.
Syed Shah Iqmal, 31, who was standing in the dock, was seen nodding as he listened to the judge’s remarks.

Earlier, in a 2-1 majority decision, Judges Datuk Azman Abdullah and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid acquitted and discharged Syed Shah Iqmal of a charge of raping a woman in 2019, while the third panel member, Judge Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, dissented and would have upheld the conviction and sentence meted out by the lower court.

The panel made the decision after allowing Syed Shah Iqmal’s final appeal against his conviction and sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment and three strokes of the cane, imposed by the Shah Alam Sessions Court.
After Judge Azman delivered the majority decision, Syed Shah Iqmal was seen weeping in the dock, while his wife, Hana Ismail, who was seated in the public gallery, was also seen crying.
On Dec 10, 2020, Syed Shah Iqmal pleaded not guilty to raping a 23-year-old woman at a condominium unit in I-City, Section 7, here, at about 1.35 am on Sept 11, 2019.
The charge was framed under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
On April 10, 2023, the Shah Alam Sessions Court acquitted and discharged him of the charge after ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case at the close of its case.
However, the Shah Alam High Court subsequently allowed the prosecution’s appeal and ordered Syed Shah Iqmal to enter his defence. — Bernama

3ce6f853e6bc3749: JOHOR BARU: Despite a nearly 25 per cent increase in raw material costs, some Deepavali traders have chosen to keep the prices of traditional Indian delicacies unchanged this year to ensure the festive treats remain affordable.
For 50-year-old R. Mages, preserving the affordability of traditional delicacies is as important as keeping the flavours and traditions of Deepavali alive.

The trader, who has been selling traditional Indian snacks and biscuits for 19 years, offers 27 varieties priced between RM25 and RM35 per container at her premises in Jalan Panti 3, Taman Bukit Tiram.
She said the cost of ingredients, including sugar, flour, margarine, ghee, butter and cooking oil, had risen, along with gas and electricity expenses.
"Despite the increases, I decided to maintain the prices so more people can afford to enjoy the treats during Deepavali.
"Orders from customers in Kuala Lumpur and Singapore have helped me cover part of the production costs, including workers' wages," she said.
Her offerings include traditional sweets and savouries, with less-sweet ladu proving particularly popular among customers who prefer a milder taste.
She said hundreds of pieces were made fresh in-house to meet daily orders, making ladu one of her best-selling items.

Meanwhile, a trader in his 60s, who wished to be known only as Indra, said business at the Deepavali bazaar in Johor Baru had been encouraging, with most of his traditional delicacies nearly sold out.
Indra, a member of the Johor Indian Business Association (JIBA), said he was keeping prices reasonable to attract customers.
"Business has been better this time compared with previous years.
"We offer three to four containers of assorted delicacies for RM100, which gives customers better value for their money," he said.
Deepavali, the festival of lights, is celebrated by Hindus to symbolise the triumph of light over darkness and good over evil.
It falls on the 20th day of the Hindu lunar month of Kartika, usually in October or November. This year, the celebration falls on Nov 8.
d7ffd68516332e71: KUALA LUMPUR: An MP today asked why millions of ringgit set aside for National Library development went unspent, while another called for a law to protect old town names such as Tanjung Penaga and Klian Pauh.

Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang) said the National Library was allocated RM19.2 million for development in 2025. She said the amount was later reduced to RM12.4 million, but government figures showed that none of it was spent.
She asked the national unity ministry to explain why the money approved by Parliament had gone unused.
Wong also asked whether public libraries were meeting people's needs, saying many open only from 9am to 5pm on weekdays, when students are in school.
She said students preparing for the SPM and STPM examinations needed affordable places to study, particularly on weekends, instead of having to spend money at cafes.
She cited her experience in Kluang, where she said libraries were packed with students after their opening hours were extended to Saturdays and Sundays.
"We have public facilities, but we are merely ticking boxes without thinking about how easily people can use them," she said during the committee-stage debate on the national unity ministry's budget.

Wong also sought details on the RM6.85 million allocated for National Library development next year and urged libraries to embrace reading trends on social media, including BookTok, to attract younger readers.
Meanwhile, Siti Mastura Muhammad (PN-Kepala Batas) proposed a law to preserve the names of historical places and allow their restoration, citing George Town's Tanjung Penaga and Taiping's Klian Pauh.

She also cited Jalan Temiang in Seremban, which was renamed after DAP founding chairman Dr Chen Man Hin, and asked why more was not being done to preserve such names. However, she did not specifically call for the towns to be renamed.
"Future generations should not only know the names of places without understanding the history and stories behind them," she said.
Siti Mastura also called for a national record of Malaysian historical artefacts, manuscripts and documents held overseas, as well as efforts to bring them home.
She sought visitor figures for the Guar Kepah Archaeological Gallery in Penang, which opened in January.
The gallery houses prehistoric human remains and artefacts discovered at the site, which dates back thousands of years.

She called for more school visits and tourism programmes to promote the gallery, as well as efforts to document local history, traditional medicine practitioners and oral accounts before such knowledge is lost.
1bfcd8baedd7edc4: MASJID TANAH: Caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the state was taking concrete steps to strengthen its energy sector by diversifying energy sources and promoting more sustainable power generation.
With more high-tech industries and data centres establishing a presence in the state, he said electricity demand would continue to rise, making a reliable energy supply crucial.
"This is particularly relevant to ensuring that the state's energy infrastructure keeps pace with its next phase of industrial growth.

"Melaka must look to the future, which is why it is important to plan ahead to meet the energy needs of tomorrow's industries," he said at the CGNEI Gas Turbine Power Committee 2026 Work Conference at the Edra Melaka Power Plant (EMPP) here today.
The conference was officiated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof and attended by 120 industry leaders, engineers and technology partners from five countries.

To meet growing energy demand, Ab Rauf said Melaka Corporation (MCorp) and Edra Power Holdings were collaborating to develop an integrated data centre ecosystem, with the aim of scaling up power capacity to two gigawatts.
He also highlighted the contribution of the 2,242-megawatt EMPP to Malaysia's electricity supply, describing it as a demonstration of Melaka's advanced energy capabilities.
As one of Southeast Asia's largest combined-cycle gas turbine power plants, EMPP played a vital role in strengthening energy security and supporting the state's industrial growth, he said.

The collaboration between MCorp and Edra Power Holdings also involves exploring the potential development of a floating storage and regasification unit in Tanjung Bidara to strengthen gas supply infrastructure and support future power generation.
Edra recently announced a proposed investment of RM6 billion, which could create more than 3,000 jobs.
Ab Rauf said the investment represented another opportunity to strengthen Melaka's energy sector, support high-value industries and generate meaningful economic benefits for the people.
On sustainable power generation, he said solar farms in Ayer Keroh, Rembia, Bemban and Masjid Tanah had an estimated combined annual electricity generation potential of 102 gigawatt-hours.
Building on this progress, Melaka was developing its first hybrid solar project, with a planned capacity of 90 megawatts and completion targeted by the end of 2027.
"We are also advancing the Sungai Udang Waste-to-Energy Project, which is expected to generate 22 megawatts of electricity when it becomes operational in 2029," he said.
Ab Rauf said these initiatives complemented the role of gas-fired power generation in ensuring a reliable electricity supply.
"Our goal is to support industrial growth through an energy system that is both reliable and sustainable," he said.
He said investment in energy infrastructure and advanced technologies must be accompanied by investment in the people who would shape the future of the energy industry.

To this end, Ab Rauf called on CGN Energy International, Edra and their industry partners to continue creating opportunities for skilled local talent, particularly young people in Melaka, through specialised training, industrial placements and meaningful career pathways.
6b82ff57df4e09d3: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Malaysia is not obligated to heed the recommendation made by major powers to raise its defence spending to 5 per cent of Gross National Product (GNP), Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin told the Dewan Rakyat today.

Khaled suggested the push for more defence spending only serves the interest of foreign powers who want neutral nations on the frontlines during major conflicts, in allusion seemingly made towards countries that are seen as hostile to China.

“There are countries recommending that we raise our defence expenditure to five per cent of GNP. The intention is that these major powers want us out in front whenever there is a clash, conflict, or war,” Khaled said in reply to William Leong (PH-Selayang).
Malaysia and Southeast Asia have long committed to a non-aligned foreign policy that had been formally codified amid geopolitical tension caused by the Cold War.
Khaled said Mindef will manage its defence budget based on its own national capabilities.

Putrajaya allocates roughly 1.0 to 1.1 per cent of national output to defence spending annually, according to Malaysian Defence, an online defence magazine. Under Budget 2026 the Ministry of Defence was allocated RM21.7 billion.

“We want to state clearly that we are not married to any major power. We are free, we are neutral, and we spend and allocate funds according to our own capability,” the minister said, adding that the country’s military doctrine is purely defensive.
“Our defence doctrine is meant to defend the nation, not to attack any country,” he said.
4bda37b5cf2dedb1: xSINGAPORE, Nov 4 — Members of the public are discouraged from rummaging through refuse bins for empty drinks containers, regardless of whether the act causes any public hygiene issue, said Minister for Sustainability and the Environment Grace Fu in Parliament yesterday.

“Apart from the potential disamenities to the wider community, there are also hygiene and safety concerns for the individuals doing so,” the minister explained in a written reply to MP Yeo Wang Ling (Punggol GRC).

The second-term MP had asked what will guide the authority’s enforcement approach towards those found removing beverage containers from public refuse bins, including in instances where no waste is scattered or no public hygiene issue is caused.

Under the Environmental Public Health (Public Cleansing) Regulations, combing through a refuse bin or removing items from it carries a fine of up to S$1,000 (RM3,181) for a first offence, with a further S$100 for each day the offence continues.

Fu noted that even before the Beverage Container Return Scheme (BCRS) was introduced, the National Environment Agency (NEA) would occasionally receive feedback on individuals rummaging through refuse bins, adding that NEA focuses first on public education to promote good hygiene practices.
And when such actions are detected, the agency takes a calibrated approach in determining whether enforcement action will be taken, she said.
“Where individuals are found rummaging through public refuse bins without leaving litter on the ground, our officers may provide an advisory.”
NEA may also refer such agencies to social agencies for further support, if they are assessed to be vulnerable individuals.

The Ministry of Social and Family Development and its community partners use the Vulnerable-in-Community Network to connect with these individuals, understand their situation and give them the support they need, the minister said.
BCRS became fully operational on Thursday (October 1), following a six-month transition period.
As at September 27, over 48 million beverage containers have been collected, with the average number of containers per transaction increasing from 2.8 in April to 8.2 in September.
Around 55 per cent of materials collected are plastics, while the remaining 45 per cent are metal, NEA shared in an update on October 1. — AsiaOne
85d3ed9e692087e4: KUALA LUMPUR: Yes Group Management Bhd is eyeing higher returns from Europe's ground transportation market through plans to buy commercial vehicles and establish a UK operating base.
Managing director Angela Mak Shau Kwan said the UK will serve as a strategic hub for the group's operations, allowing it to supply vehicles to key Western European destinations.

"UK is an international hub for the European market. When we purchase a vehicle there, we are not only renting it out in the UK, but also to Germany and Western Europe," she said at a press conference after its prospectus launch.
Mak illustrated that if the group acquires commercial vehicles, including 16-to-21-seater Sprinter coaches, each vehicle is estimated to cost between £110,000 and £140,000.
She said the investment may offer better rental income potential compared with similar investments in Malaysia.
"With the same amount of investment, if we purchase a coach in Malaysia, it may cost RM600,000 to RM700,000, with rental rates of around RM2,000 per day.
"In the UK, we can charge up to £5,000 to £6,000 per day," she said.
Mak said the expansion will also reduce the group's reliance on local third-party ground transportation providers, which currently charge margins of between eight and 10 per cent.
"Our ground transportation services are currently assigned to local partners in Europe, whom we have worked with for years. Of course, they also need to earn a margin.
"We want to reduce costs across all segments. These partners charge margins of between eight and 10 per cent, which we could save by establishing our own office there," she said.
Mak added that the group will primarily focus on Western Europe, including popular destinations such as Paris, London, Italy and Amsterdam.
She said vehicle deployment will depend on demand and rental costs, as Eastern European markets offer rental rates about 20 per cent cheaper.
Meanwhile, Mak said rising oil prices have increased travel costs, but the group will pass the additional expenses on to corporate clients rather than absorb them.
"When we give quotations to clients, we base them on the prevailing currency exchange rates and oil prices.
"As long as we provide our clients with the previous quotation and updated oil prices in black and white, we will automatically top up the difference," she said.
She said clients will be given time to obtain management approval for the additional costs.
On demand, Mak said the group's meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) business continue to grow, supported by the expansion of Malaysia's industry.
"According to our independent market research report, the MICE industry's value has increased almost threefold, from RM6 billion in 2022 to around RM18 billion in 2025," she said.
She acknowledged that geopolitical tensions had affected European incentive travel earlier this year, resulting in some trips being postponed.
However, she said the group's order book shows that demand for European tours was recovering.
"Europe will always be a branded destination. It ranks among the preferred destinations for high-performing employees," she said.
Mak said the group's customised incentive travel approach involves designing itineraries based on the demographic profiles of corporate clients' employees.
She said the group also considered participants' ethnic composition, including the proportions of Chinese, Indian and Malay travellers, to ensure activities and arrangements suited each group.
Mak said this approach allowed the company to create more personalised experiences rather than offer standard travel packages.
Separately, Yes Group plans to establish Yes Academy, which will initially offer structured training programmes rather than diploma or degree qualifications.
"Currently, there is no one offering these courses yet. We believe there is very good potential for us to nurture the next generation and equip them with the relevant industry skills," she said.
The group is targeting a break-even point of 100 students annually, requiring approximately three to four classes.
Mak said the first intake was expected to begin nine months after the group's listing, in its next financial year.
Yes Group, which operates under the Yes Travel brand, has been operating since 2008, focusing on customised corporate incentive travel and event planning and management solutions.
The group operates exclusively on a business-to-business model, focusing on multinational corporations, government-linked companies and publicly listed companies rather than the retail travel market.
The group is scheduled to list on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market on Nov 26.

8eefcf662cd17d67: I wanted to be a beacon of black feminist love; my friends and family teased me for being a sellout We had been together 20 years, had two children and had a customary marriage with our village sub-county two years ago without any real plans for a church wedding. 32b56e628ac70447: MACAU: Casino heiress Laurinda Ho, daughter of the late gambling tycoon Stanley Ho, reportedly splashed out more than RM5,700 on a lavish meal for her family at an exclusive Hong Kong restaurant.
The 35-year-old posted a video on social media showing her dining with her mother, businesswoman Ina Chan, 73, and three other relatives at the hard-to-book eatery.
The restaurant's set menu costs around HK2,200 (about RM1,142) per person, including service charge.
For five guests, the total bill came to roughly HK11,000 (around RM5,714), not including drinks or extra dishes.
Laurinda explained that she arranged the meal as a special treat for her mother after waiting a long time to get a table.
"The wait was absolutely worth it. Every dish was interesting and incredibly delicious," she said.
The video showcased a lineup of decadent dishes, including crispy-skinned milk-fed porcine topped with black truffle and caviar, king crab, and clay pot rice made with fresh mushrooms.
The family also enjoyed dedicated one-to-one service throughout the evening.

Besides the impressive feast, viewers quickly spotted the eye-catching jade bangle worn by Laurinda's mother. Reports say the piece was a gift from her late husband and was valued at 30 million yuan (around RM18.4 million) at the time—with its present value believed to have doubled.
2991ebd4629df9b7: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government has no specific plans to develop state-owned land on Pulau Jerejak, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said.
He, however, said several private development proposals had been submitted, covering mixed developments as well as the provision of infrastructure and recreational facilities on the island.

In his reply at the state legislative assembly, Chow said a Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL) for a bridge construction site connecting Persiaran Bayan Indah near Queensbay to Pulau Jerejak was approved in 2023.
The licence covers an area of 2.02 acres (0.817ha) and has been renewed annually through 2026 at a yearly fee of RM12,300.
He was responding to a question by Pulau Tikus assemblyman Joshua Woo on the state government's or private landowners' plans to develop Pulau Jerejak.
The state administration noted that all proposed developments on Pulau Jerejak remained private developer-led initiatives.
"Their actual implementation remains subject to planning approvals, land matters and compliance with all technical and statutory requirements established by the relevant authorities," he added.
Pulau Jerejak was formerly a leprosy asylum, quarantine station and penal colony.
About 85 per cent of the island is gazetted as a protected forest reserve and cannot be developed.
02359a796f382fad: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump acknowledged that the war in Iran played a role in Republicans' losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, as Democrats prepared to take control of both the US House and Senate and challenge his legislative agenda.
In an interview with Fox News, Trump said Democrats would send legislation he considered "insane" to his desk and that he would veto it.

"They'll send over things that are insane, and I'll veto them," he said. "And after a couple of months of vetoes, they'll call and they'll say, 'How do we get this stuff done?' And we'll work together."

Trump said the war in Iran had weighed on Republican candidates, even as voters backed his handling of it. "I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time people understood the importance of what I've done with Iran," he said.
5d2e3e532691cfd8: BEIJING: Apple began on Wednesday a long-delayed trial rollout of in-house artificial intelligence tools for Chinese users, playing catch-up to homegrown smartphone makers in a major market for the US giant.
The on-device features dubbed "Apple Intelligence" were first released in the US and other countries in autumn 2024, marking the firm's first major push into generative AI.

But strict Chinese regulatory requirements for the fast-evolving technology have held back its launch there – as well as the fact that models from Google and OpenAI, which Apple has used elsewhere to boost its own AI capabilities, are not available in the country.

Apple, which has largely stayed out of the global AI investment frenzy, announced it will work with a Chinese partner – Alibaba's Qwen – to integrate more powerful AI features into devices alongside its own basic AI offerings.
Wednesday's trial rollout is restricted to developers, but public access to Apple Intelligence services in China will come in December, the company said in a statement at the weekend.
The long-anticipated Chinese rollout of Apple Intelligence "fills a long-standing gap in Apple's AI offering", said Ivan Lam, a senior analyst at Counterpoint Research.
However, it does not necessarily give the Californian company "a significant advantage" in a crowded market, Lam said.
The initial release includes 18 AI features, from live translation of phone calls to tools for summarising and proofreading messages, but not the latest upgrade of iPhone assistant Siri.
Chinese regulations require AI service providers to register with the country's internet watchdog, and there are requirements to use local data centres and process data domestically.
Apple only secured regulatory approval in July, after reportedly holding talks with Chinese tech firms including Alibaba, Baidu, ByteDance and Tencent about partnerships on Apple Intelligence.
Major US AI firms, including Google, OpenAI and Anthropic, have either banned Chinese users or restricted access to their services and are unlikely to secure regulatory clearance.

Working with local partners on Apple Intelligence "signifies a structural concession by Apple regarding its pricing and defining power over the AI experience in the Chinese market", Zhang Yi, founder of research firm iiMedia, told AFP.
Apple's delay in introducing AI tools in China was not due to lags in research and development, but rather "compliance costs", he said.

Despite reporting a 21 per cent increase in revenue in the Greater China region, which includes Hong Kong and Taiwan, for the past quarter, Apple's new CEO John Ternus still faces significant challenges in an evolving market.
According to research firm Omdia, more than 110 million iPhones in China can support Apple Intelligence, providing a foundation for quick adoption – but competition is fierce.
"Chinese mobile phone manufacturers and internet companies are actively developing AI features and agent ecosystems," Zhong Xiaolei, a senior analyst at Omdia, told AFP.
9771953a3bc61423: Supporters of South Carolina Democratic Senate candidate Annie Andrews cheer during her election night watch party on Nov. 3, 2026, in Charleston, S.C. AP Photo/Mic SmithVoters turned out in massive numbers on Election Day to hand Democrats control of Congress, in a sweeping snub of President Donald Trump and Republicans. Democrats won several statewide races in places long considered GOP bastions, including races that were considered insurmountable even weeks ago. Democrats took control of the House and Senate, flipping Senate seats in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina, Kansas and Ohio. The results reflected broad dissatisfaction across the country with Trump, his agenda and the candidates he had endorsed. The Conversation’s senior politics editor, Alfonso Serrano, spoke on election night with Charlie Hunt, a scholar at Boise State University who studies Congress and elections. It was obviously a strong showing for Democrats on Election Day, something that was even evident in the margin of some Democratic losses. What does it tell you, for example, that democratic socialist Angie Nixon fought a competitive race for the Senate in Florida? There is this big uniform shift toward the Democrats that we’re seeing really across virtually all kinds of locations and geographies and counties. What I think is particularly notable here, and something we were on the lookout for in this election, and we’re seeing it, is the substantial shift in the Hispanic vote from 2024 in places like Texas and Florida, where you’re getting these 30-to-35 point shifts from how Donald Trump performed in 2024. That was a big part of what helped him win, and it seems like it has snapped right back and even farther in the other direction. This is what made Florida, I think, closer than a lot of folks thought. It’s what put a number of really, really right-leaning districts in play, particularly in South Florida. And it looks like it is going to help Democrats keep the number of seats they had in Florida in the House that they had before the election, which is incredible when you consider that Florida did this mid-decade gerrymander to try to get them out of a bunch of those seats. Some rural areas of the country were also more competitive than expected, like North Carolina’s 11th Congressional District, where Democrat Jaime Ager flipped a conservative district. What does that tell you? It’s definitely an indicator of at least one of these two things. One is just really massive Democratic turnout across the board. Regardless of where they live, Democrats were so enthusiastic and energized to turn out that they did so across all different types of districts and counties. It could also be an indicator of some cross-party voting, where Republicans are crossing over in some cases and voting for the Democrat. I don’t imagine there’s a ton of that, but in a lot of these close districts, and if you’ve got enough of those folks in places like Texas, it really does make a big difference, those small shifts. I think we’re probably also likely to see, and we saw some of this in the exit polling, a major shift in independent voters, unaffiliated voters, toward the Democrats, whereas in 2024 they had been closer to Trump. I’d like to go back to turnout briefly. Turnout looks like it was strong across the country. In Georgia, for example, Election Day’s turnout was on pace to beat turnout in the 2024 presidential elections. That’s unprecedented, at least in modern elections. In Texas, for example, in some counties we saw James Talarico getting as many raw votes as Kamala Harris did in a presidential election. This isn’t a very political science term, but that’s insane. In a midterm election you typically see 10% or 15% less turnout than you would in a presidential election. But Democrats voted in presidential-level numbers in a lot of these really key areas, and that’s explaining how they’re able to overperform at levels we haven’t seen in at least 20 years. Voters cast their ballots on Election Day at the Cross Insurance Center polling location on Nov. 3, 2026, in Bangor, Maine. Joe Raedle/Getty Images Elon Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars supporting Republican candidates, including some US$200 million in Texas to elect Ken Paxton for the Senate, who lost. What does that tell you about the influence of political spending? Republican PACs, super PACs and billionaire donors like Elon Musk may have raised more money compared to Democrats, but Democratic candidates themselves outraised Republican candidates through donors that gave directly to their campaigns. This is important for a couple of reasons. Number one, because candidates get much better rates on TV ad buys than outside spenders. And so they get more bang for their buck when they’re spending on advertisements, which is the most expensive component of any campaign. And more to the point, that is an indicator of sort of dedicated grassroots donors who turn into voters, whereas Musk gets one vote at the end of the day. And there is no amount of money that can make up for a really flawed candidate like Ken Paxton. And more to the point, a lot of this money, once you get into the tens, the hundreds of millions of dollars, a lot of the research talks about the diminishing returns that you get on that. Going from zero dollars spent to $10 million spent, that’s a very different kind of campaign. But once you go from $500 million to $510 million, that’s not going to get you a whole lot more votes. Any final thoughts? The territory that Democrats covered is unbelievable. The South Carolina Senate race went to Annie Andrews, the Democrat, which was unfathomable even a few months ago. Mississippi still appears to be somewhat in play. The blue wave turned into something approaching a tsunami. I think a lot of Democrats saw the polling and didn’t want to believe it or couldn’t bring themselves to believe it. But some of this late polling seems to have gotten things on the mark. What we’ve seen in these midterm elections is a massive rebuke of the last two years of the Trump administration, and a sort of blue wave of epic proportions toward the Democrats, the likes of which we haven’t seen in 20 or more years. It’s a huge confirmation of the approach that Democrats took in this election. 1a8728b2f86bf0ee: SINGAPORE, Nov 4 — Three new MRT stations on the Thomson-East Coast Line (TEL) and Downtown Line (DTL) — Bedok South, Sungei Bedok and Xilin — will open for passenger service on December 26.
The first two stations are part of the TEL stage 5 (TEL5), while Xilin MRT station is part of the Downtown Line 3 Extension (DTL3e).

“These new stations will stitch together two major train corridors, give commuters in the East new routes, and faster journeys,” said Minister for Transport Jeffrey Siow at the Singapore Urban Mobility Week today.

Illustrating this, Siow pointed out that residents in the eastern region will be able to take the TEL continuously into the city centre, up north to Woodlands, and soon, conveniently across the Johor Strait into Malaysia.
The three new stations — Bedok South, Sungei Bedok and Xilin — sit between Expo and Bayshore stations. — Graphic courtesy of Singapore’s Land Transport Authority
The new stations are also expected to enhance access to employment nodes such as Changi Business Park and Tampines Regional Centre.
Meanwhile, Sungei Bedok interchange will also enable commuters to transfer between the TEL and DTL, providing more travel options and strengthening the resilience of our rail network.

LTA said that the opening of TEL5 will put over 240,000 households within a 10-minute walk of a TEL station, while the opening of DTL3e will see 220,000 households within a 10-minute walk of a DTL station.
It projected savings of between 10 and 25 minutes for commuters travelling between the eastern region and other parts of Singapore.
The agency gave the example of commuters travelling from Havelock to Changi Business Park via TEL and DTL, which would take around 45 minutes, as compared to the present 70 minutes.
Those travelling from Marine Parade to Tampines via TEL and DTL can also expect time savings of up to 10 minutes compared to today.
Estimated travel time savings for commuters following the opening of Bedok South, Sungei Bedok and Xilin stations. — Table courtesy of Singapore’s Land Transport Authority
The upcoming opening of the TEL stations also completes the line’s five-stage planned opening, with 29 operational stations over 42.8km.
When the future Changi Terminal 5 extension is completed in the mid-2030s, the TEL is expected to serve about one million daily commuters.

The opening of Sungei Bedok interchange and Xilin station, connecting the north-western and eastern parts of the island through the city centre, will extend the line to over 44.6km and 37 operational stations. — AsiaOne

5647e36759a50f22: JASIN: Barisan Nasional candidate for Sungai Rambai, Jezlee Pit, has unveiled a five-year development plan, dubbed Mewajah Sungai Rambai Lima Tahun, to accelerate development in the area and improve residents' socioeconomic well-being.

He said the development programme was expected to transform Sungai Rambai into a more advanced and competitive area without compromising its identity and unique character as an agricultural hub, particularly for padi cultivation, which remained a source of livelihood and part of the local community's heritage.
"Through this plan, I have set a five-year target for implementing development initiatives to ensure people in the area enjoy a comfortable and harmonious life.

The proposed clinic, to be built on a three-hectare site along Jalan Parit Putat in Sungai Rambai, aims to provide more comfortable and quality healthcare facilities that meet the needs of the local population.

He said the proposed clinic was among the initiatives pursued by the Melaka government through former Sungai Rambai assemblyman Datuk Siti Faizah Abd Azis to improve healthcare facilities for people in the area.

Ahmad said Jezlee's experience as a former penghulu in Sungai Rambai and Merlimau, as well as his previous role as Melaka Penghulu Council chairman, had given him an understanding of the needs of the local community.
"I am confident that our former penghulu can carry this forward and continue the efforts to ensure the project is realised," he said.
9238456686cd589d: KUALA LUMPUR: SME Bank is targeting 100 individuals from B40 households for technical and vocational education and training (TVET) under its Zero to Hero 3.0 programme.
The programme aims to improve employability and financial resilience among lower-income communities.

Rolled out in collaboration with Giatmara Sdn Bhd and Zurich General Takaful Malaysia Bhd, it will provide industry-recognised training in welding and metal fabrication, alongside financial education, industry exposure and employment support.
Recognised by Bank Negara Malaysia under its iTEKAD Employment initiative, the Zero to Hero 2.0 will run between 2026 and 2027.

SME Bank chief executive officer Samad Majid Zain said by equipping participants with in-demand technical skills and connecting them with employers, the programme provides a practical pathway towards meaningful and sustainable employment."
The programme builds on two previous cohorts, which supported 30 participants in 2022 and another 60 in 2024.
All 90 participants secured employment, representing a 100 per cent employment rate.
For the latest cohort, participants are expected to earn monthly salaries ranging from RM1,800 to RM6,000 upon securing employment.

Giatmara will oversee participant selection, deliver competency-based training, facilitate industry certification and coordinate job placements, while monitoring participants' progress throughout the programme.
Zurich General Takaful will fund the programme, provide participants with one year of takaful protection and deliver practical financial education to help them manage their finances.

Zurich General Takaful chief executive officer Shamsul Azman said; "Creating lasting financial resilience requires more than technical skills, it demands strong partnerships and a shared commitment to empowering individuals for a more secure and brighter future."
The iTEKAD initiative, introduced by Bank Negara in 2020, has benefited more than 14,000 low-income microentrepreneurs nationwide.

More than RM94 million in social finance funds and about RM77 million in financing and investments have been channelled through the initiative, contributing to the creation of more than 2,400 employment opportunities.

SME Bank said its own iTEKAD Ishraf programme had supported nearly 1,000 asnaf entrepreneurs since 2020, with participants collectively generating about RM40 million in income and creating more than 400 jobs.
The Zero to Hero 3.0 programme also supports the National TVET Policy 2030 and Financial Sector Blueprint 2027-2030.
eefed511e9b74162: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Corporation (JCorp) and private equity firm CVC Capital Partners are reportedly seeking buyers for the KFC and Pizza Hut fast-food restaurant businesses operated by QSR Brands (M) Holdings Bhd.

A financial portal, citing sources, reported that international investment bank Citi is handling the sale process, identifying foreign investors, particularly those from West Asia, as potential candidates.
Several parties reportedly expressed interest, although discussions remain at an early stage and may not necessarily result in a transaction.
The asking price is said to be one of the key sticking points after one potential buyer reportedly withdrew because the valuation was too high.
According to sources cited in the report, the asking price is around RM4 billion.
JCorp and CVC, together with the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), control the business through Massive Equity Sdn Bhd.
Massive Equity fully owns QSR Brands, which operates the KFC chain in Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei and Cambodia, as well as Pizza Hut outlets in Malaysia and Singapore.
According to the latest information on QSR Brands' website, the group operates more than 850 KFC restaurants and over 500 Pizza Hut outlets across the region.
JCorp holds a 55.63 per cent stake in Massive Equity, while Melati Asia Holdings Ltd owns 44.19 per cent. The remaining interest is held by several individuals.
Melati Asia is jointly owned by EPF, with a 51 per cent stake, and CVC, with 49 per cent.

The report quoted JCorp group senior general manager of corporate communications Hasnina Hafiz as saying that the group remained focused on developing competitive and resilient businesses across its portfolio.
She said JCorp adopted a disciplined approach in evaluating investment opportunities to create sustainable long-term value.
QSR Brands remained an important component of JCorp's investment portfolio, while its improved performance reflected progress in operational efficiency and competitiveness, she said.
Any material developments would be announced through the appropriate channels at the appropriate time, she added.
The statement neither confirmed nor denied the reported plans to sell the business. CVC and Citi declined to comment further.

QSR Brands' performance had previously come under pressure from changing consumer spending patterns, rising operating costs and boycott campaigns triggered by the Israel-Palestine conflict since October 2023.
However, JCorp said in June that QSR Brands' revenue for the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025, rose 19 per cent to RM3.85 billion.

QSR Brands also returned to profitability following measures to improve operational efficiency, optimise its portfolio, enhance customer experience and tighten cost controls. The amount of profit was not disclosed.
OneCredit data showed that QSR Brands' revenue increased from RM4.81 billion in 2022 to RM4.87 billion in 2023, before declining 33.7 per cent to RM3.23 billion in 2024.
The company recorded a pre-tax profit of RM49.58 million in 2022, followed by pre-tax losses of RM66.2 million in 2023 and RM332.67 million in 2024.
In 2012, JCorp, together with EPF and CVC, acquired QSR Brands and its subsidiary KFC Holdings (M) Bhd in a transaction valued at RM5.2 billion.
The transaction, completed in February 2013, resulted in both companies being delisted and taken private.

16d56b2c98ab68e8: KUALA LUMPUR: Low Zi Yu is just 16 but has already set her sights on competing at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics (LA28).
Her coach, Rosman Razak, believes her ambitious mindset makes her a precious gem in the national team.

This is also why the national women's doubles chief has assured that world junior champion Zi Yu and Noraqilah Maisarah Ramdan will remain together as a permanent pairing in their bid to qualify for LA28.
World No. 4 Pearly-Thinaah look assured of their spots, with a nation allowed a maximum of two entries in the women's doubles event, where 16 pairs qualify for the Olympics.
With world No. 26 Ong Xin Yee-Carmen Ting struggling to make an impact, the fast-rising world No. 42 pairing of Zi Yu-Noraqilah is seen as the leading prospect to join Pearly-Thinaah at LA28.

"That's what makes her special. I think that despite being only 16 years old, she is one of those players with a very different mindset. She has high ambitions and knows exactly what she wants to achieve," said Rosman.
"She is also very mature. That's a very good quality because we want players with that kind of mentality.

"She has even told me directly, 'Coach, I want this, I want that. I want to achieve certain things.' But these are all positive ambitions, not negative demands. When people ask whether she wants to compete at the Olympics, she says yes, which is a good thing.
"Setting a target as big as the Olympics means she understands that she has to improve in many areas, make a lot of sacrifices and know what she needs to do to achieve that goal.
"As coaches, we are very pleased to see this attitude."
Rosman added that Zi Yu, who won the world junior girls' doubles title with Genevie Lim in Cairo last month, is a player who leads by example.

"Zi Yu doesn't just talk about her ambitions, she backs them up with action. Since joining the national team, I believe she has improved in every aspect of her game. Her presence has also pushed the other players to raise their game," said Rosman.
"Given that she is still young, her attitude and approach have had a positive influence on the team and helped lift the overall standard."
Zi Yu's success in Cairo also raised expectations that the Segamat-born player could be given a chance on the World Tour, but Rosman has ruled out the idea of splitting the partnership.
"I will not break up Zi Yu and Aqilah as they are already very good," Rosman said.
"Next year, the Olympic qualification points will come into play. At the moment, Zi Yu is already ranked just outside the top 40. So, making changes to the pairings now would be quite risky.
"The other players are not yet at a sufficiently high level, and breaking into the top 32 with a new pairing would be extremely difficult if we were to start all over again.
"Ideally, at least for the Olympic qualification campaign, we need to have two or three pairs capable of challenging for places in the competition."
Zi Yu and Noraqilah, 19, showed their pedigree when they toppled Japan's world No. 5 pair Rin Iwanaga-Kie Nakanashi during the Uber Cup campaign in Horsens, Denmark.
They also finished runners-up at the Super 100 Baiji Masters, while reaching the quarter-finals of the Super 300 Taiwan Open and Super 500 Australian Open this year.
Meanwhile, Zi Yu's efforts at the World Junior Championships were also rewarded on Tuesday, when she received RM10,000 from the Johor BA (JBA) and an additional RM3,000 from Eu Jin Sdn Bhd.
Zi Yu and Sarawak-born Genevie also received G-Shock watches as tokens of appreciation from the private company.
